text: Meeting deadlines is a skill that improves with practice. Good time management starts with breaking a large project into smaller, daily tasks. This makes the work feel less overwhelming and helps you track your progress. Prioritization is also key; identify which tasks are most important and do those first. Furthermore, you should practice scope management by avoiding the temptation to add extra features or details that were not part of the original plan. Finally, if you realize you are falling behind, communicate with your team or supervisor early. A quick update allows others to adjust their expectations, and they might even offer help. Proactive communication is always better than a last-minute surprise.
